title: MILL ROW — Rain gardens and a shared street for an old shopping lane, 14 deliverables

config.text:
# MILL ROW

- Project: Rain gardens and a shared street for an old shopping lane.
- Site boundary: 80 m east–west by 12 m north–south.
- Site area: 960 m².
- Coordinate origin: southwest corner; x east, y north.
- Level datum: local datum, expressed in m.
- Fixed arrangement, south to north: South Walk, Shared Lane, Rain Garden, Shop Forecourt.
- Existing identity: red-brown brick shopfronts, cream stone lintels, dark timber doors, gray stone curbs and rectangular gray paving.
- Existing retained assets: entrances E1–E4, trees T1–T4 and stone curbs.

## Zone allocation

| Zone | y limits | Area | Physical role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| South Walk | 0–2 m | 160 m² | Continuous pedestrian route |
| Shared Lane | 2–6 m | 320 m² | Shared walking and cycling |
| Rain Garden | 6–8 m | 160 m² | Four storage beds and four shop crossings |
| Shop Forecourt | 8–12 m | 320 m² | Shop arrival, deliveries and short stays |

## Levels and drainage

- Longitudinal fall: 0.5% eastward.
- Shared Lane crossfall: 1% northward.
- Shop Forecourt crossfall: 1% southward.
- Catchment: 800 m².
- Design rainfall: 25 mm.
- Runoff coefficient: 0.90.
- Storage volume: 18 m³.
- Drawdown target: 24 hours.
- Storage beds: four, each 15 m by 2 m; total 120 m².
- Bed floors: horizontal within each bed.
- Design ponding depth: 150 mm.
- Downstream freeboard: 50 mm.
- A-A section: x = 17 m, looking east.
- A-A floor: 99.675 m.
- A-A downstream rim: 99.875 m.
- A-A design water level: 99.825 m.

## Access and existing assets

- South Walk clear width: 2 m.
- Garden crossings: four, each 2 m wide.
- Utility corridor: y = 0–1.5 m, full street length.
- Tree protection radius: 1 m around each recorded trunk.
- Movement pattern: walking and cycling along the street; shop deliveries stop within Shop Forecourt.

## Plant palette

| Code | Plant |
| --- | --- |
| CE | Carex elata |
| JE | Juncus effusus |
| IS | Iris sibirica |

## Fixed wording and scene states

- Site name: MILL ROW.
- Zone names: South Walk; Shared Lane; Rain Garden; Shop Forecourt.
- Scene states: dry afternoon; rainy afternoon; dusk.
- Paired viewpoint: eastward, identical camera position for dry and rainy conditions.
- Additional viewpoint: westward at dusk.
- Sequence duration: 10 seconds.
- Presentation length: at least eight pages.

## Plant palette

| Code | Species | Allocation |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Existing street character

- Northern frontage: two-story red-brown brick buildings with cream stone lintels and dark timber shop doors at E1–E4.
- Ground finish: rectangular gray stone paving and gray stone curbs.
- Existing tree rhythm: four trees between the shop entrances.
- Shopfront identity elements: brick color, lintel profile, timber doors and stone curb material.

steps.userMessage:
MILL ROW | Rain gardens and a shared street for an old shopping lane

We are renewing MILL ROW so residents can walk, cycle, visit the shops and pause beside planted rain gardens. The project covers an 80 m by 12 m street, totaling 960 m². Retain the four shop entrances, four existing trees, stone curbs and brick shopfronts recorded in the attachments. The direction is fixed: a continuous southern footway, a central shared walking and cycling lane, a rain garden band and a northern shop forecourt. Develop the ground finishes, planting and places to pause within this arrangement.

The four zones are South Walk, 160 m²; Shared Lane, 320 m²; Rain Garden, 160 m²; and Shop Forecourt, 320 m². The street falls east at 0.5%; the lane and forecourt fall toward the garden at 1%. Four level-bottomed beds provide 120 m² of planted storage within the garden band, with 150 mm design ponding and at least 50 mm freeboard at each downstream edge. The drainage brief fixes an 800 m² catchment, 25 mm design rainfall, runoff coefficient 0.90, 18 m³ storage and a 24-hour drawdown target. Maintain a 2 m clear southern footway and four 2 m shop connections across the garden band. Print "MILL ROW" and the four zone names on the masterplan and planting and materials schedule; repeat the plant names Carex elata, Juncus effusus and Iris sibirica in both.

Audience: residents who walk and cycle, shop operators and street maintenance staff, supporting the street layout decision and the detailed design brief.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the project facts and fixed zone allocation. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. 03-site-records.en.md contains coordinates, levels, drainage conditions, access records and the planting palette. street-constraints.png provides the boundary, entrances, trees, utility corridor and drainage positions. street-section-dry.png provides the fixed cross-section and bed geometry at section A-A. street-section-rain.png provides the design water level at that same section. mill-row-existing.png records the brick shopfront, stone curb and paving character to retain. everyday-street-reference.png provides the atmosphere of walking, cycling and shop deliveries. rainy-street-reference.png provides the atmosphere of a rainy shopping afternoon.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page site analysis and zone area schedule, with the four zone names, areas, paving types, shade methods, proposed simultaneous occupancy and three plant names
2. One masterplan with north arrow, scale bar, boundary, four zones, eight fixed access and tree positions, bed footprints, planting labels, seating and lighting positions
3. One grading and drainage plan with spot levels, flow arrows, four inlets, four overflows, the five drainage brief figures and the geometric storage calculation
4. Two cross-sections at A-A: one dry and one at design ponding, with surface levels, bed floor, water level and clear route widths
5. One rain garden construction detail sheet with inlet, sediment pocket, level bed, underdrain, overflow and an adjacent shop connection
6. One planting plan with species codes, quantities, bed allocation and four retained trees
7. One planting and materials schedule with the site name, four zone names and areas, species codes, full plant names, quantities, planting sizes and paving build-ups
8. One shop access and maintenance plan with four entrance connections, threshold levels, the southern footway, cycling movement, delivery stopping and sediment-removal access
9. Three street perspectives: a dry afternoon and rainy afternoon from the same eastward viewpoint, and a dusk view looking west, with shop use, planting and route continuity
10. One 10-second street sequence moving from dry conditions to design ponding at the eastward viewpoint
11. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the analysis, plans, sections, detail, schedule and perspectives, with the fixed arrangement on page one

Acceptance:
- The site analysis, masterplan, planting and materials schedule and presentation repeat South Walk 160 m², Shared Lane 320 m², Rain Garden 160 m² and Shop Forecourt 320 m²; the masterplan shows the 80 m by 12 m boundary, north arrow and scale bar.
- The masterplan, planting plan, planting and materials schedule and presentation repeat the analysis's Carex elata, Juncus effusus and Iris sibirica; the planting plan and schedule use CE, JE and IS with matching quantities. The masterplan and schedule print MILL ROW and all four zone names.
- The grading and drainage plan, both A-A sections and construction detail agree on the 0.5% longitudinal fall, 1% crossfalls and recorded inlet and overflow positions. At A-A, label the bed floor 99.675 m and downstream rim 99.875 m; the rainy section labels water level 99.825 m and ponding depth 150 mm. The drainage plan shows four 15 m by 2 m beds and the storage calculation 120 m² × 0.15 m = 18 m³.
- The masterplan and shop access and maintenance plan retain entrances E1–E4, trees T1–T4 with their 1 m protection radii, and the 1.5 m southern utility corridor. Both plans dimension the 2 m southern footway and four 2 m garden crossings; the access plan repeats all four recorded threshold levels and locates delivery stopping and sediment-removal access.
- The three perspectives and 10-second sequence use the masterplan's shopfronts, beds, crossings, seating and planting. The dry and rainy perspectives share one eastward camera position; the dusk perspective looks west and uses the masterplan's lighting positions.
- The presentation contains at least eight pages, identifies the fixed four-band arrangement on page one, and repeats the analysis's zone areas and three plant names alongside the completed drawings and the dry, rainy and dusk perspectives.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
